Himani, you ask why I always serve everyone before myself? Let your Gopika Ammamma tell you.
When I was ten, we lived in a joint family in Thrissur with eleven children. Whatever came in, we shared. If I got a mango, I cut it into pieces for all the cousins, without anyone asking.
It felt warm. Six of us girls shared one room.
But once, I badly wanted to learn the veena. The money went to my cousin's school fees instead. Nobody asked me, and I said nothing. I thought wanting something for myself was wrong.
Years later, my mother said, "You should have told us." And I realised I'd never learned to say what I wanted.
